INTRODUCTION

In pursuance of the provisions of National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) Act 2020 (14 of 2020), the Indian Medicine Central Council (IMCC) Act 1970 (48 of 1970) has been repealed and all the provisions of the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) has been come into force with effect from the 11th day of June 2021. Under the provisions of section 59 (2) of NCISM Act 2020 the Central Government has constituted the Commission and four Autonomous boards on the same day. Medical standards, requirements and other provisions of the IMCC Act 1970 and the rules and regulations made thereunder shall continue to be in force and operate till new standards or requirements as specified under new act or rules and regulations made thereunder come into force. However, the provisions of concerned regulations which are inconsistent with the provisions of NCISM Act 2020 shall not be applicable.

Constituted 11 June 2021 · NCISM Act, 2020

The standard for Indian medicine.

Four systems · one commission

Four traditions.
One nation's heritage of healing.

NCISM brings India's recognised systems of medicine under a single regulatory umbrella — each preserved in its distinct identity, each held to the same modern standard.

आयुर्वेद The science of life

Ayurveda

Rooted in the Vedas, Ayurveda ranks among the world's oldest systems of holistic medicine — a discipline of the upaveda tradition, drawn chiefly from the Atharva-Veda.

Explore Ayurveda यूनानी The Graeco-Arabic tradition

Unani

Refined through centuries of scholarship across Greece, Persia and India, Unani medicine traces its teachings to Hippocrates and Galen, carried forward by physicians such as Avicenna.

Explore Unani सिद्ध The perfected science

Siddha

Founded by the Siddhars of southern Tamil Nadu, this tradition unites Kayakarpam and Muppu — the universal salt — in a system built for rejuvenation and long life.

Explore Siddha सोवा-रिग्पा The science of healing

Sowa-Rigpa

Practised across the Himalayan belt — Ladakh, Sikkim, Arunachal and Himachal — Sowa-Rigpa diagnoses through pulse analysis and urinalysis, guided by the Four Tantras.

Explore Sowa-Rigpa
